verdict.desc: The market reopens after Labor Day into a risk-off, oil-driven tape. Over the long weekend the U.S. and Iran traded fresh strikes — the U.S. hit three Iranian oil tankers, Saudi Aramco facilities were reportedly struck — and crude is pinned near six-week highs (WTI ~$92.5, Brent ~$97), lifting the 10-year yield to ~4.80% and reviving September-hike fears. CPI lands Thu 9/11 and the FOMC is 9/15–16, both inside a normal spread window, and the VIX is ticking up off its 2026 lows. Composite gap-risk is WARM (56) and P(≥1% gap) is 39% — above the 35% trigger — so GREEN is locked out. The scanner boarded one name (REPX, a Type C breakout); everything else is stand-aside. Do not open new premium into a live war plus a CPI/FOMC week, or push DTE past the event window.

focus.jbig: Post-holiday reopen · oil near $92 · CPI Thu, FOMC next week
focus.jtag: Fresh U.S.–Iran strikes over the weekend keep crude at six-week highs; yields up, futures mixed-to-lower into a big data week
focus.jnote: The tape reopens after Labor Day under pressure. Over the weekend the U.S. struck three Iranian oil tankers after Iran fired ballistic missiles at two Navy warships, Saudi Aramco facilities were reportedly hit, and the market is increasingly pricing a prolonged Mideast conflict. Crude is at six-week highs — WTI ~$92.5, Brent ~$97 — and Goldman raised its Brent/WTI forecasts by $5 to $85/$80 for December. The oil bid pushed the 10-year yield to ~4.80%, reviving talk of a September rate hike, and equity futures are mixed-to-lower (Dow futures the weakest). The VIX, which hit a 2026 low of ~14.2 in mid-August, is ticking back up toward ~15.3–15.7. This is a live, open-ended conflict stacked on top of a CPI/FOMC week — not a premium-selling setup.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, MPC) and Defense (LMT, RTX, NOC) keep the fundamental bid — the oil supply fear lifts energy, conflict-demand lifts defense. The scanner did surface one energy breakout (REPX, Type C), but note this is a two-sided war trade: a Hormuz-reopening or de-escalation headline gaps energy straight back down. Treat energy strength as a war premium, not a clean trend.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive growth and fuel-sensitive transports are the pressured groups — higher oil and a 4.80% 10-year weigh on both. But selling bear calls into a VIX that’s rising off its lows, with CPI in 3 days and an FOMC next week that could reprice the curve either way, is exactly the blow-up 4-VAL exists to prevent. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite 56 is squarely WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 39% is above the 35% trigger — either one alone locks out GREEN. Layer on a live U.S.–Iran military exchange with oil near $92, an upcoming CPI (Thu 9/11) and FOMC (9/15–16) both inside a normal DTE, and the overnight tail is skewed and hard to size. The scanner boarded just one Type C breakout (REPX). Stand down on new credit spreads, or if you must be positioned, use 7-DTE that clears CPI and the FOMC and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: The scanner boarded REPX as a Type C ATH breakout: it reports the breakout held ~2 sessions above the $41.21 pivot on ~2.5x volume, one S/R layer at the pivot, ATM spread $0.05 and OI 2,829 — a clean liquidity pass, next earnings ~Nov 4 (well outside DTE). Caveat you must verify: live quotes this morning show REPX around the $41–42 area with a 52-week high near $41–42, not the ~$43 print in the scanner record — so confirm the stock is actually trading above its prior all-time high before trusting the breakout. Even if it is, this is an oil-beta name on a RED day: the same Iran/Hormuz premium powering the move can gap it down on any de-escalation headline. Grade A per the scanner, but the tape argues for caution.

August CPI · Thu 9/11 — the cleaner Fed signal before the FOMC, and with oil near $92 feeding inflation fear an upside surprise is more likely than usual. A hot print stacked on the oil shock is the worst-case macro combination.
FOMC · Tue–Wed 9/15–16 — a live hike-or-hold meeting; a stronger August jobs report (payrolls +162K) already revived September-hike odds. Any spread must expire before this.
Oil & the 10-year — WTI near $92.5 keeps inflation fear alive; the 10Y is already back to ~4.80%. A renewed oil pop compounds pressure on stocks and hardens the hike case.
Oracle earnings tonight; single-stock landmines — ORCL reports AMC 9/8, and pharma is bleeding on Novartis’ two failed studies (AMGN, LLY, IONS). Keep every spread clear of its name’s catalyst.
